kill_fact: Moat erosion is confirmed by primary sources and there is no evidence of durable pricing power. On the Q3 2026 call (2026-10-22) management said domestic broadband ARPU (revenue per user) is still DECLINING year over year. The decline only 'narrowed sequentially by 190 basis points', and connectivity revenue fell 2.6% and connectivity EBITDA fell 4.4%, with fixed wireless and fiber 'irrational pricing' named as the cause. Management is buying share back with price cuts, a five-year price guarantee and free mobile lines, which is the opposite of pricing power. Return on invested capital is about 6.1% TTM (FMP key-metrics, 10-Q dated 2026-09-30), below any reasonable cost of capital, and Q3 2026 total revenue was $29.30B against $31.20B a year earlier. The cheapness (about 5x EV/EBITDA, an 18.8% FCF yield) is a structural price for a melting core, not mispricing.
corrections: ROIC: the record's bear case cites 6.8%. FMP key-metrics TTM to 2026-09-30 gives 6.1%, so returns are worse than stated, not 'rising'.

Buybacks: these are not merely 'reported on hold' (press, 2026-11-08). The CFO said on the Q3 2026 call (2026-10-22) that repurchases were paused as of July 1 and expected 'to remain in place at least through the separation' (mid-2027). The paused per-share accretion lever is company-confirmed.
Q3 2026 FCF of $4.2B included 'favorable timing impacts that we expect to reverse in the fourth quarter' (CFO, 2026-10-22). The $17.1B TTM FCF anchor is modestly flattered.
Live price is $25.61 (2026-11-16), against $24.51 in the record. Net debt of $79.77B (borrowings $87.37B less cash $7.60B, 2026-09-30) VERIFIES.
